post_rebuild_reparse.method: civds.combat.read_combat_constant_value() run directly against the rebuilt ROM's ARM9 image for every one of the 11 registered constants (the rebuilt image no longer matches the pinned exact-ROM profile by design, so `civds combat summarize` correctly refuses it; this step re-verifies with the same reader used by that command)

byte_level_verification.method: read the raw 4-byte instruction word at the fortified-in-city-bonus offset directly out of the rebuilt ROM file
byte_level_verification.conclusion: only the immediate byte changed; opcode, condition code, S-bit, and both register fields are bit-for-bit identical, confirming the patch scheme (replace byte 0 of a rotate=0 8-bit-immediate ARM data-processing instruction) is surgically precise

conclusion: Three guarded combat constants (two tied to debug-print strings, high confidence) were patched from the real ROM in one manifest, applied to an extracted workspace, rebuilt into a new ROM, and re-parsed - confirming exactly the three targeted constants changed to their requested values and all eight other registered constants were untouched. This proves the combat-constant patch capability end to end as a real balance-modding tool, not just a static analysis claim.
